# [STORY] As a maintainer, I want an accurate, consistently linked backlog and one shared agent contract

## User Story
**As a** maintainer
**I want** the backlog's hierarchy and the agent work contract to be accurate, consistently linked, and shared by every agent tool
**So that** the project board shows real state, and the rules can't drift between Claude Code and Antigravity

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given any Story or Task, when it is inspected, then it declares its parent and that parent lists it back — in the markdown body and as a native GitHub sub-issue, with the two agreeing
- [x] Given a closed issue, when its acceptance criteria are read, then no box is left unchecked without a stated rescope, and no issue is closed without evidence the work exists
- [x] Given a new issue is created from a template, when it is filled in, then the template already carries the parent section, labelled child entries, the do-not-close-unchecked rule and the Notes-length rule
- [x] Given Antigravity opens this repo, when it loads its configuration, then it reads the same contract, the same skills, and equivalent hooks and MCP servers as Claude Code

## Definition of Ready
- [x] Meets [Definition of Ready](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_READY.md)

## Story Points
**Estimate:** 5

## Notes
All four Tasks closed and verified against a fresh fetch of the live API, not against this issue's own text.

AC1: 0 linkage problems across all 187 issues; native parent links 35 to 159.
AC2: 24 closed issues had unchecked criteria — 20 ticked with evidence, 2 rescoped under ADR-015, #120 reopened because no commit referencing it exists. Only #177 remains unchecked, waiting on a human merging PRs.
AC3: all four templates pass the same audit script that found the original drift.
AC4: `AGENTS.md` symlinked to `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.agents/skills`, verified to survive a clean clone; Antigravity's graphify hook adapter tested against every input shape.

Known inconsistency, not introduced here: reopening #120 leaves Story #77 closed with one open child Task. #77 closed in Sprint 6, so it wants a decision — reopen it, or give post-Sprint-6 chores a new maintenance Story under #76.
